records.order: row_index ascending, each row_index distinct and < rows

reference_note: THE STIMULUS CARRIES A REAL TIE AT HIGH LANES: 40017 and 48000 both hold the row's maximum, so `ref_out.bin`'s single lane is 40017 -- FIRST-max pinned against a tie, not a vacuous uniqueness. THE NEGATIVE CONTROLS ARE PART OF THE CONTRACT, AND THERE ARE FOUR: (1) a last-max implementation answers 48000 against these same bytes and must not match `ref_out.bin`; a run that still matches cannot have taken the tie. (2) an f16-DEGRADED FINAL COMBINE answers 40032 or 40016 -- 40017 = 625*64 + 17 is not fp16-representable (ULP 32 at [32768, 65536)) -- so a kernel whose `b*64 + l` island collapsed out of f32 cannot match either; a run that still matches cannot have degraded. The tie lanes are high ON PURPOSE: the original 100/5000 stimulus sat inside fp16's exact-integer range and could not see (2) at all. (3) THE PADOFF CONTROL: the row's pads past V=49155 hold 0.0 -- the production shape, the lm-head's zero-pad columns -- and the real lanes sit BELOW ZERO, so a kernel that maxes the RAW row answers a pad lane; only `x + padoff` (the staged offset row, -inf past V) keeps the answer on the real lanes. A kernel that lets a pad lane win answers PAD_V-adjacent garbage, never 40017. (4) THE ROW-FEEDBACK CONTROL: `in_table_ptr.sparse` holds ONLY the answer row and the pad row (row 49155, randn bytes, deliberately unlike production's zeros) -- every other row expands to zero, so a gather that reads any row but the clamped answer answers zeros and diverges from the byte-exact row pin; and the sentinel leg (an all-NaN logits row, bound by the test over these same bytes) must land the clamp on the PRESENT pad row, whose nonzero bytes prove the landing row by name.
